Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeParser

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-code formats

The shared record and table parser layer for fixed machine serializations.
This factors the one- and two-work-tape constructions of [AB09, §1.4].

## Main definitions

* `Turing.CodeFormat` — a table grammar, its laws and its fallback.
* `Turing.actionBitsK` / `Turing.codeReadActionK` — records for any work-tape count.
* `Turing.CodeTable2` — the shared 27-record two-work-tape table.
* `Turing.oneTapeFormat` — the one-work-tape instance and public decoder wrappers.

## Main results

* `Turing.CodeFormat.decode_serialize_pad` — padded decoding recovers the machine.
* `Turing.CodeFormat.canonical_eq` — scanning computes its canonical serialization.
* `Turing.CodeFormat.numStates_decode_le` — the guarded decoded-size bound.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, pp. 19-20.)
-/

namespace Turing


/-! ## Transition records -/

/-- The serialization of a transition record lists the input move, each work-tape write
and move in tape order, the output, and the successor state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def actionBitsK {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  signBits a.inputTape ++
    (List.finRange k).flatMap
      (fun i => optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2) ++
    optBoolBits a.output ++ optStateBits a.state

/-- Read an optional work-tape write and its head move. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadWork (xs : List Bool) :
    Option ((Option (Option Bool) × SignType) × List Bool) := do
  let (wr, xs) ← codeReadWrite xs
  let (wm, xs) ← codeReadSign xs
  pure ((wr, wm), xs)

/-- Read a transition record with a vector of `k` work-tape actions. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    Option (Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1)) × List Bool) := do
  let (im, xs) ← codeReadSign xs
  let (ws, xs) ← codeReadVec codeReadWork k xs
  let (out, xs) ← codeReadOutput xs
  let (q, xs) ← codeReadState (n + 1) xs
  pure (⟨im, ws, out, q⟩, xs)

/-- Skip a work-tape write and move, enforcing their field grammar. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipWork (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
  (codeSkipPair (fun _ _ => true) xs).bind (codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b))

/-- Skip a transition record for `k` work tapes, checking the successor state bound. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let xs ← codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b) xs
  let xs ← codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork k xs
  let xs ← codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b) xs
  codeSkipState (n + 1) xs

/-- Reading a serialized work-tape action recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadWork_append (p : Option (Option Bool) × SignType) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadWork ((optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2) ++ xs) = some (p, xs) := by
  rcases p with ⟨wr, wm⟩
  simp only [codeReadWork, List.append_assoc, codeReadWrite_append, codeReadSign_append,
    bind, Option.bind, pure]

/-- Reading a serialized transition recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadActionK_append {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadActionK k n (actionBitsK a ++ xs) = some (a, xs) := by
  rcases a with ⟨im, ws, out, q⟩
  have hv : ∀ ys, codeReadVec codeReadWork k
      ((List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i => optOptBoolBits (ws i).1 ++ signBits (ws i).2) ++ ys) =
        some (ws, ys) :=
    codeReadVec_append codeReadWork (fun p => optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2)
      codeReadWork_append k ws
  simp only [actionBitsK, List.append_assoc, codeReadActionK, codeReadSign_append, hv,
    codeReadOutput_append, codeReadState_append, bind, Option.bind, pure]

/-- A successful work-tape read consumes exactly the serialization of its result. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadWork_sound (xs : List Bool) (p : Option (Option Bool) × SignType)
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadWork xs = some (p, rest)) :
    xs = (optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2) ++ rest := by
  simp only [codeReadWork, bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨wr, r₁⟩, h₁, ⟨⟨wm, r₂⟩, h₂, h⟩⟩ := h
  simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  rw [codeReadWrite_sound xs wr r₁ h₁, codeReadSign_sound r₁ wm r₂ h₂]
  simp [List.append_assoc]

/-- A successful transition read consumes exactly the serialization of its result. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadActionK_sound {k n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1)))
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadActionK k n xs = some (a, rest)) :
    xs = actionBitsK a ++ rest := by
  simp only [codeReadActionK, bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨im, r₁⟩, h₁, ⟨⟨ws, r₂⟩, h₂, ⟨⟨out, r₃⟩, h₃, ⟨⟨q, r₄⟩, h₄, h⟩⟩⟩⟩ := h
  simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  rw [codeReadSign_sound xs im r₁ h₁,
    codeReadVec_sound codeReadWork (fun p => optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2)
      codeReadWork_sound k r₁ ws r₂ h₂,
    codeReadOutput_sound r₂ out r₃ h₃, codeReadState_sound r₃ q r₄ h₄]
  simp [actionBitsK, List.append_assoc]

/-- Erasing the work-tape reader result gives the work-tape skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseWork (xs : List Bool) : (codeReadWork xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipWork xs := by
  simp only [codeReadWork, codeSkipWork, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def, pure,
    Option.map_some]
  rw [← codeEraseWrite xs, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  simpa only [Option.map_eq_bind, Function.comp_def] using codeEraseSign p.2

/-- Erasing the transition reader result gives the transition skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadActionK k n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipActionK k n xs := by
  have hv (ys : List Bool) :
      (codeReadVec codeReadWork k ys).map Prod.snd = codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork k ys := by
    rw [codeEraseVec]
    exact congrArg (fun r => codeSkipRepeat r k ys) (funext codeEraseWork)
  simp only [codeReadActionK, codeSkipActionK, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def, pure,
    Option.map_some]
  rw [← codeEraseSign xs, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  rw [← hv p.2, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  rw [← codeEraseOutput p.2, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  simpa only [Option.map_eq_bind, Function.comp_def] using codeEraseState (n + 1) p.2

/-- Every `k`-work-tape record has at least `4 * k + 5` bits. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Each work tape contributes four bits. The input move and output contribute
four more, and the successor-state field contributes at least one. -/
lemma codeActionK_length {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    4 * k + 5 ≤ (actionBitsK a).length := by
  have hs (s : SignType) : (signBits s).length = 2 := by cases s <;> rfl
  have ho (b : Option Bool) : (optBoolBits b).length = 2 := by
    rcases b with _ | b
    · rfl
    · cases b <;> rfl
  have hw (b : Option (Option Bool)) : (optOptBoolBits b).length = 2 := by
    rcases b with _ | (_ | b)
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · cases b <;> rfl
  have hq : 1 ≤ (optStateBits a.state).length := by
    cases a.state <;>
      simp only [optStateBits, unaryFin, List.length_cons, List.length_append,
        List.length_replicate, List.length_nil] <;> omega
  have hv : 4 * k ≤ ((List.finRange k).flatMap fun i =>
      optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2).length := by
    simpa using codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange k)
      (fun i => optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2) 4
      (fun i _ => by simp [hs, hw])
  simp only [actionBitsK, List.length_append, hs, ho]
  omega

/-- The work-symbol function reading `w₀` on tape `0` and `w₁` on tape `1`,
for the fixed table enumeration of `Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize`. -/
def workPair (w₀ w₁ : Option Bool) : Fin 2 → Option Bool :=
  fun j => if j = 0 then w₀ else w₁

/-- Serialization of one two-work-tape transition record: the input-head move,
then each work tape's optional write and move in tape order, then the emission
and the successor state — `Turing.actionBits` with a second work-tape record. -/
def actionBits₂ {n : ℕ} (a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  signBits a.inputTape ++
    optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes 0).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes 0).2 ++
    optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes 1).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes 1).2 ++
    optBoolBits a.output ++ optStateBits a.state

/-- The fixed one-work-tape serialization agrees with the generic record serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma actionBits_eq_actionBitsK {n : ℕ} (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    actionBits a = actionBitsK a := by
  simp [actionBits, actionBitsK, List.finRange_succ, List.append_assoc]

/-- The fixed two-work-tape serialization agrees with the generic record serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma actionBits₂_eq_actionBitsK {n : ℕ} (a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    actionBits₂ a = actionBitsK a := by
  simp [actionBits₂, actionBitsK, List.finRange_succ, List.append_assoc]

/-- The fixed one-work-tape skipper agrees with the generic skipper at `k = 1`. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeSkipAction n xs = codeSkipActionK 1 n xs := by
  have h1 (ys : List Bool) : codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork 1 ys = codeSkipWork ys := by
    cases h : codeSkipWork ys <;> simp [codeSkipRepeat, h]
  simp only [codeSkipAction, codeSkipActionK, h1, codeSkipWork, bind, Option.bind_assoc]

/-! ## Table formats -/

/-- A machine-code format specifies a transition-table grammar under the shared
state-count and initial-state header, together with its parser laws and fallback. [AB09, §1.4] -/
structure CodeFormat where
  /-- the coded machines -/
  Code : Type
  /-- the transition table of a machine with `n + 1` states -/
  Table : ℕ → Type
  /-- one less than the number of states -/
  numStates : Code → ℕ
  /-- assemble a machine from its state count, initial state and table -/
  assemble : (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1) → Table n → Code
  /-- the format's fixed serialization -/
  serialize : Code → List Bool
  /-- the fixed serialization of a table -/
  tableBits : {n : ℕ} → Table n → List Bool
  /-- the table reader -/
  readTable : (n : ℕ) → List Bool → Option (Table n × List Bool)
  /-- the erased table reader -/
  skipTable : ℕ → List Bool → Option (List Bool)
  /-- the minimum number of table bits per state (the up-front guard constant) -/
  guard : ℕ
  /-- the machine denoted by every malformed string -/
  fallback : Code
  numStates_assemble : ∀ n q t, numStates (assemble n q t) = n
  serialize_assemble : ∀ n q (t : Table n),
    serialize (assemble n q t) = pairEncode n.bits (unaryFin q ++ tableBits t)
  assemble_surj : ∀ M, ∃ n q t, assemble n q t = M
  readTable_append : ∀ n (t : Table n) xs, readTable n (tableBits t ++ xs) = some (t, xs)
  readTable_sound : ∀ n xs (t : Table n) rest,
    readTable n xs = some (t, rest) → xs = tableBits t ++ rest
  readTable_erase : ∀ n xs, (readTable n xs).map Prod.snd = skipTable n xs
  tableBits_length : ∀ n (t : Table n), guard * (n + 1) ≤ (tableBits t).length

namespace CodeFormat

variable (F : CodeFormat)

/-- Parse a machine and retain its all-true padding; check the table-length guard
before reading any state-indexed table entries. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def parseFull (xs : List Bool) : Option (F.Code × List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode xs
  let n := codeBitsNat bits
  if bits ≠ n.bits then none else do
    if F.guard * (n + 1) > rest.length then none else do
      let (q, rest) ← codeReadFin (n + 1) rest
      let (table, rest) ← F.readTable n rest
      if rest.all id then pure (F.assemble n q table, rest) else none

/-- Decode every string, choosing the format's fallback on any malformed input. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def decode (xs : List Bool) : F.Code := ((F.parseFull xs).map Prod.fst).getD F.fallback

/-- Check the same header, table-length guard and padding as the parser,
retaining only the unconsumed suffix. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def scan (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode xs
  let n := codeBitsNat bits
  if bits ≠ n.bits then none else do
    if F.guard * (n + 1) > rest.length then none else do
      let rest ← codeSkipFin (n + 1) rest
      let rest ← F.skipTable n rest
      if rest.all id then pure rest else none

/-- Return the consumed prefix when scanning succeeds and the fallback's serialization
when scanning fails. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def canonical (xs : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (F.scan xs).casesOn (F.serialize F.fallback) fun tail => xs.take (xs.length - tail.length)

/-- Parsing a serialization followed by true padding recovers the machine and padding. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The doubled header recovers the canonical state-count bits. The table-length
bound discharges the early guard; the initial-state and table inverse laws recover
the assembled machine and leave the replicated true suffix, which passes the padding test. -/
theorem parseFull_serialize_pad (M : F.Code) (m : ℕ) :
    F.parseFull (F.serialize M ++ List.replicate m true) =
      some (M, List.replicate m true) := by
  obtain ⟨n, q, t, rfl⟩ := F.assemble_surj M
  have hp (a b c : List Bool) : pairEncode a b ++ c = pairEncode a (b ++ c) := by
    simp [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
  rw [F.serialize_assemble, hp]
  unfold parseFull
  rw [pairDecode_pairEncode]
  dsimp only [bind, Option.bind]
  rw [codeBitsNat_bits]
  simp only [ne_eq, not_true_eq_false, ↓reduceIte]
  have hlen := F.tableBits_length n t
  simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate] at *
  rw [if_neg (by omega)]
  simp only [List.append_assoc, codeReadFin_append, F.readTable_append,
    List.all_replicate, id_eq, ite_self, ↓reduceIte, pure]

/-- Decoding a serialization followed by arbitrary true padding recovers the machine. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_serialize_pad (M : F.Code) (m : ℕ) :
    F.decode (F.serialize M ++ List.replicate m true) = M := by
  simp only [decode, parseFull_serialize_pad, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]

/-- Every successful parse expresses the input as the decoded serialization and suffix. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Decompose the successful parse and use the field and table soundness equations.
The canonical state-count check reconstructs the doubled header, giving exactly
the machine serialization followed by the retained suffix. -/
theorem parseFull_sound (xs : List Bool) (M : F.Code) (tail : List Bool)
    (h : F.parseFull xs = some (M, tail)) : xs = F.serialize M ++ tail := by
  unfold parseFull at h
  obtain ⟨⟨bits, rest⟩, hp, h⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
  dsimp only at h
  split at h
  · contradiction
  next hb =>
    have hb : bits = (codeBitsNat bits).bits := not_not.mp hb
    split at h
    · contradiction
    next _ =>
      simp only [bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨q, r₁⟩, hq, ⟨⟨table, r₂⟩, ht, h⟩⟩ := h
      split at h
      next hpad =>
        simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
        rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
        have htable := F.readTable_sound _ _ _ _ ht
        dsimp only at htable
        rw [F.serialize_assemble, eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode xs bits rest hp,
          codeReadFin_sound rest q r₁ hq, htable]
        simp only [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
        congr 1
        exact congrArg (List.flatMap fun b : Bool => [b, b]) hb
      · contradiction

/-- The erased scanner returns exactly the suffix retained by the full parser. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Push suffix projection through the parser's binds and branches. The initial-state
and table erasure laws replace their readers by the corresponding skippers; the
header checks and final padding test are unchanged. -/
theorem scan_full (xs : List Bool) : F.scan xs = (F.parseFull xs).map Prod.snd := by
  simp only [scan, parseFull, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def]
  congr 1
  funext p
  dsimp only
  split <;> try simp only [Option.map_none]
  split <;> try simp only [Option.map_none, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def]
  have h (q : Fin (codeBitsNat p.1 + 1) × List Bool) (t : F.Table (codeBitsNat p.1) × List Bool) :
      (if t.2.all id then some (F.assemble (codeBitsNat p.1) q.1 t.1, t.2) else none).map
          Prod.snd = (if t.2.all id then some t.2 else none) := by split <;> rfl
  simp only [pure, h]
  rw [← codeEraseFin _ _, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext q
  rw [← F.readTable_erase, ← codeErase_bind]

/-- The scanner-based canonical prefix equals the serialization of the decoded machine. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem canonical_eq (xs : List Bool) : F.canonical xs = F.serialize (F.decode xs) := by
  unfold canonical decode
  rw [scan_full]
  cases h : F.parseFull xs with
  | none => rfl
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨M, tail⟩
    simp only [Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]
    rw [F.parseFull_sound xs M tail h]
    simp

/-- The decoded serialization is no longer than the input or the fixed fallback,
whichever is longer. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem serialize_decode_length_le (α : List Bool) :
    (F.serialize (F.decode α)).length ≤ max α.length (F.serialize F.fallback).length := by
  rw [← F.canonical_eq]
  unfold canonical
  cases F.scan α with
  | none => exact Nat.le_max_right _ _
  | some tail => exact (List.length_take_le' _ _).trans (Nat.le_max_left _ _)

/-- The guarded table-size lower bound for the decoded machine is bounded by the
input length or the fallback length, whichever is larger. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem numStates_decode_le (α : List Bool) :
    F.guard * (F.numStates (F.decode α) + 1) ≤
      max α.length (F.serialize F.fallback).length := by
  have hsize := F.serialize_decode_length_le α
  obtain ⟨n, q, t, h⟩ := F.assemble_surj (F.decode α)
  rw [← h, F.serialize_assemble, length_pairEncode, List.length_append] at hsize
  rw [← h, F.numStates_assemble]
  have htable := F.tableBits_length n t
  omega

/-- A failed full parse decodes to the format's fallback. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_of_parseFull_none (α : List Bool) (h : F.parseFull α = none) :
    F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  simp [decode, h]

/-- A failed table-length guard decodes to the fallback before table recursion. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_of_guard_lt (α bits rest : List Bool) (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest))
    (hg : rest.length < F.guard * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)) : F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  simp [decode, parseFull, hp, hg]

end CodeFormat

/-! ## Two-work-tape tables -/

/-- A two-work-tape transition table is indexed by state, input read, and both work reads. [AB09, §1.4] -/
abbrev CodeTable2 (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → Option Bool → Option Bool → Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))

/-- Serialize all two-work-tape table entries in state, input, work-0, work-1 order. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeTable2Bits {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) : List Bool :=
  (List.finRange (n + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
          actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)

/-- Read the 27 two-work-tape transition records for every state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadTable2 (n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (CodeTable2 n × List Bool) :=
  codeReadVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 2 n)))) (n + 1)

/-- Skip the 27 two-work-tape transition records for every state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipTable2 (n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (List Bool) :=
  codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipActionK 2 n) 3) 3) 3)
    (n + 1)

/-- Reading a serialized two-work-tape table recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadTable2_append {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadTable2 n (codeTable2Bits t ++ xs) = some (t, xs) :=
  codeReadVec_append _ _ (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
    (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
      (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _ codeReadActionK_append _ _) _ _) _ _) _ _ _

/-- A successful two-work-tape table read consumes exactly its serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadTable2_sound {n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (t : CodeTable2 n) (rest : List Bool)
    (h : codeReadTable2 n xs = some (t, rest)) : xs = codeTable2Bits t ++ rest :=
  codeReadVec_sound _ _ (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
    (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
      (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _ codeReadActionK_sound _ _ _) _ _ _) _ _ _)
    _ _ _ _ h

/-- Erasing the two-work-tape table reader result gives the corresponding skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseTable2 (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadTable2 n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipTable2 n xs := by
  have ht := codeEraseVec
    (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 2 n)))) (n + 1) xs
  simp only [codeEraseSymbols, codeEraseActionK] at ht
  exact ht

/-- Every two-work-tape table has at least 351 bits per state. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Every record has at least 13 bits. Sum this lower bound over each of the
three possible symbols on each of three reads, giving 27 records and 351 bits
per state; then sum over the state enumeration. -/
lemma codeTable2Bits_length {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) :
    351 * (n + 1) ≤ (codeTable2Bits t).length := by
  have hr : ∀ a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1)), 13 ≤ (actionBitsK a).length :=
    fun a => by have := codeActionK_length a; omega
  have h := codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange (n + 1))
    (fun q => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
          actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 351 (by
      intro q _
      have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
        (fun inp => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
          ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
            actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 117 (by
          intro inp _
          have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
            (fun w₀ => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
              actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 39 (by
                intro w₀ _
                simpa using codeFlatMap_length
                  ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
                  (fun w₁ => actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 13 (fun _ _ => hr _))
          simpa using h)
      simpa using h)
  simpa [codeTable2Bits] using h

/-! ## One-work-tape instance -/

private lemma codeReadActionK_one_append {n : ℕ} (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadActionK 1 n (actionBits a ++ xs) = some (a, xs) := by
  rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; exact codeReadActionK_append a xs

private lemma codeReadActionK_one_sound {n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1)))
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadActionK 1 n xs = some (a, rest)) :
    xs = actionBits a ++ rest := by
  rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; exact codeReadActionK_sound xs a rest h

private lemma codeEraseActionK_one (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadActionK 1 n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipAction n xs := by
  rw [codeEraseActionK, codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK]

/-- The one-work-tape `CodeTM` format has nine records per state and guard 81. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The frozen record serialization is the generic one at one work tape. Nested
vector and symbol-reader laws provide table inversion, soundness and erasure;
summing the nine-bit record bound over the nine records gives guard 81. -/
def oneTapeFormat : CodeFormat where
  Code := CodeTM
  Table := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → Option Bool → Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))
  numStates := CodeTM.numStates
  assemble := fun n q t => ⟨n, ⟨q, fun s inp w => t s inp (w 0)⟩⟩
  serialize := CodeTM.serialize
  tableBits := fun {n} t => (List.finRange (n + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
        actionBits (t q inp w)
  readTable := fun n =>
    codeReadVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 1 n))) (n + 1)
  skipTable := fun n =>
    codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipAction n) 3) 3) (n + 1)
  guard := 81
  fallback := codeFallback
  numStates_assemble := fun _ _ _ => rfl
  serialize_assemble := fun _ _ _ => rfl
  assemble_surj := by
    rintro ⟨n, q, tr⟩
    refine ⟨n, q, fun s inp w => tr s inp (fun _ => w), ?_⟩
    show CodeTM.mk n ⟨q, fun s inp w => tr s inp (fun _ => w 0)⟩ = CodeTM.mk n ⟨q, tr⟩
    congr 1
    congr 1
    funext s inp w
    apply congrArg (tr s inp)
    funext i
    exact congrArg w (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
  readTable_append := fun _ _ _ =>
    codeReadVec_append _ _ (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
      (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _ codeReadActionK_one_append _ _) _ _) _ _ _
  readTable_sound := fun _ _ _ _ h =>
    codeReadVec_sound _ _ (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
      (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _ codeReadActionK_one_sound _ _ _) _ _ _)
      _ _ _ _ h
  readTable_erase := fun n xs => by
    have ht := codeEraseVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 1 n))) (n + 1) xs
    simp only [codeEraseSymbols, codeEraseActionK_one] at ht
    exact ht
  tableBits_length := fun n t => by
    have hr : ∀ a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1)), 9 ≤ (actionBits a).length := fun a => by
      rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; have := codeActionK_length a; omega
    have h := codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange (n + 1))
      (fun q => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
          actionBits (t q inp w)) 81 (by
        intro q _
        have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
          (fun inp => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
            actionBits (t q inp w)) 27 (by
              intro inp _
              simpa using codeFlatMap_length
                ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
                (fun w => actionBits (t q inp w)) 9 (fun _ _ => hr _))
        simpa using h)
    simpa using h

/-- Total decoding: every malformed string denotes the fixed fallback. -/
def codeDecode (xs : List Bool) : CodeTM :=
  oneTapeFormat.decode xs

/-- The total decoder satisfies the required exact padded round-trip law. -/
lemma codeDecode_serialize_pad (M : CodeTM) (m : ℕ) :
    codeDecode (M.serialize ++ List.replicate m true) = M :=
  oneTapeFormat.decode_serialize_pad M m

/-- The erased parser: accept exactly the strings the parser accepts, returning only the unconsumed all-true suffix. -/
def codeScan (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
  oneTapeFormat.scan xs

/-- The canonical serialization of the machine a string denotes: the consumed prefix on scanner success, the fallback machine's serialization otherwise. -/
def codeCanonical (xs : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  oneTapeFormat.canonical xs

/-- The suffix scanner computes exactly the fixed serialization of the decoded machine. -/
lemma codeCanonical_eq (xs : List Bool) : codeCanonical xs = (codeDecode xs).serialize :=
  oneTapeFormat.canonical_eq xs

end Turing
```

```
/-

Authors: Seyoon Ragavan

import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeFormat
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Nondeterministic
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.MathlibBridge

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Codes for nondeterministic machines

The nondeterministic counterpart of `TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding`'s
code layer ([AB09, §1.4], extended to NDTMs as [AB09, §3.2] requires for the
nondeterministic time hierarchy): a coded normal form `Turing.CodeNDTM`, its
fixed scheme-independent serialization, the representation-scheme laws
(`Turing.NDMachineCode`), and the effective form with a canonizer
(`Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode`). Phase P3.3 of
`AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md`; the consumers — the clocked universal NDTM of
[AB09, Exercise 2.6] at linear overhead (decision CH34-Q8) and the lazy
diagonalization of [AB09, Theorem 3.2] — are
`TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.NTimeHierarchy`.

**Status: proved (phase P3.3).** The effective scheme existence and the
padded round-trip law are proved. The canonizer has an arbitrary length-only
time bound, as required by the audited contract.

## Design

* **The coded normal form has two work tapes** (`NDTM 2 Bool`), not one: the
  deterministic `Turing.CodeTM` is one-work-tape because the chapter-1
  robustness conversion eats a quadratic slowdown anyway, but phase P3.3's
  whole point (decision CH34-Q8) is **linear** overhead, and the
  guess-then-verify tape reduction ([BGW70]-style, stated as
  `Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear` in the consumer module)
  delivers linear overhead into **two** work tapes — one for the guessed
  display sequence, one replaying the verified tape — while the one-work-tape
  target is not known to suffice at linear cost.
* **The serialization mirrors `Turing.CodeTM.serialize` record for record**:
  the same `signBits`/`optOptBoolBits`/`optBoolBits`/`optStateBits` fields,
  with a second work-tape record per action (`Turing.actionBits₂`) and the
  table enumerated over the choice bit first (`false` then `true`), then
  states in `Fin` order, then the input read and the two work reads each over
  `none`, `some false`, `some true`.
* **The scheme laws are verbatim mirrors**: total decoding (property 1),
  recovery under arbitrary `true`-padding (property 2 — infinitely many
  representations, which [AB09, Theorem 3.2]'s proof uses to pick a large
  index), and the canonizer tying `decode` to effective semantics (the
  chapter-1 audit's Argument-A exclusion, inherited by construction).

## Main definitions

* `Turing.CodeNDTM`, `Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM` — the coded two-work-tape
  normal form. [AB09, §1.4, §3.2]
* `Turing.actionBits₂`, `Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize` — the fixed serialization.
* `Turing.NDMachineCode`, `Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode` — the scheme laws
  and the effective scheme. [AB09, §1.4]

## Main results

* `Turing.NDMachineCode.decode_encode` — decoding recovers the machine
  (skeleton-time proof, mirror of `Turing.MachineCode.decode_encode`).
* `Turing.exists_effectiveNDMachineCode` — an effective scheme exists
  (proved; phase P3.3).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, §2.1.2, Exercise 2.6; §3.2.)
* [BGW70] R. Book, S. Greibach, B. Wegbreit, *Time- and tape-bounded Turing
  acceptors and AFLs*, JCSS 4(6), 1970. (Cited through [AB09]; no external
  text is required for this audit.)

## Item-8 appendix

The fixed `workPair` and `actionBits₂` definitions now live verbatim in
`CodeFormat`. The nondeterministic format instance remains a later fill obligation.

**Fill appendix.** The item-8 obligation above is now discharged by the private
`ndFormat` instance: two consecutive two-work-tape tables, false choice first,
with guard 702. The shared format decoder supplies padding tolerance and
`CodeFormat.exists_canonizer` supplies the arbitrary-time canonizer.
-/

namespace Turing

/-- The coded normal form of a nondeterministic machine: a binary-alphabet
NDTM with **two** work tapes and state space `Fin (numStates + 1)` (never
empty). Two work tapes, not one, because the guess-then-verify tape reduction
achieves linear overhead into two tapes (see the module docstring). Mirrors
`Turing.CodeTM`. [AB09, §1.4, §3.2] -/
structure CodeNDTM where
  /-- one less than the number of states (so the state space is never empty) -/
  numStates : ℕ
  /-- the underlying two-work-tape nondeterministic machine -/
  tm : NDTM 2 Bool (Fin (numStates + 1))

/-- The bundled machine of a coded nondeterministic machine. -/
def CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM (M : CodeNDTM) : FinNDTM Bool where
  k := 2
  State := Fin (M.numStates + 1)
  tm := M.tm

/-- The **fixed, scheme-independent** canonical serialization of a coded
nondeterministic machine, mirroring `Turing.CodeTM.serialize`: the state count,
the initial state, then the full two-table transition list in the fixed
enumeration order — the choice bit (`false` then `true`) outermost, then
states in `Fin` order, then the input read and the two work reads each over
`none`, `some false`, `some true`. This is the target format of
`Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode.canonizer`. -/
def CodeNDTM.serialize (M : CodeNDTM) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (Nat.bits M.numStates)
    (unaryFin M.tm.q₀ ++
      ([false, true] : List Bool).flatMap fun b =>
        (List.finRange (M.numStates + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
          ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
            ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
              ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
                actionBits₂ (M.tm.tr b q inp (workPair w₀ w₁)))

/-- The algebraic laws of a representation scheme for coded nondeterministic
machines, mirroring `Turing.MachineCode` [AB09, §1.4]: a total decoding
(property 1), an encoding, and recovery under arbitrary `true`-padding
(property 2 — every machine has infinitely many representations, which the
lazy diagonalization of [AB09, Theorem 3.2] uses to pick large indices). -/
structure NDMachineCode where
  /-- encode a machine as a binary string, `⌞N⌟` -/
  encode : CodeNDTM → List Bool
  /-- decode any binary string to a machine (total by type: property 1) -/
  decode : List Bool → CodeNDTM
  /-- a code followed by any amount of `true`-padding decodes to the machine
  (property 2: infinitely many representations) -/
  decode_encode_pad : ∀ M m, decode (encode M ++ List.replicate m true) = M

/-- Decoding a code recovers the machine ([AB09, §1.4]; padding by zero
symbols). Skeleton-time proof, mirroring `Turing.MachineCode.decode_encode`. -/
theorem NDMachineCode.decode_encode (c : NDMachineCode) (M : CodeNDTM) :
    c.decode (c.encode M) = M := by
  simpa using c.decode_encode_pad M 0

/-- An *effective* representation scheme for nondeterministic machines: the
algebraic laws together with a (deterministic) machine of this development
computing the fixed serialization of the decoded machine — the mirror of
`Turing.EffectiveMachineCode`, with the same Argument-A rationale: the target
`Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize` is scheme-independent, so a scheme whose `decode`
has noncomputable meaning admits no canonizer. -/
structure EffectiveNDMachineCode extends NDMachineCode where
  /-- a machine computing the fixed serialization of the decoded machine -/
  canonizer : FinTM Bool
  /-- the canonizer's time bound (arbitrary here; universal-machine constants
  absorb its value at each fixed code) -/
  canonizerTime : ℕ → ℕ
  /-- the canonizer computes `serialize ∘ decode` -/
  canonizer_computes :
    canonizer.ComputesFunInTime (fun α => (decode α).serialize) canonizerTime

/-- The nondeterministic code format consists of the false-choice and true-choice
two-work-tape tables, in that order, with a silent one-state fallback. [AB09, §1.4, §3.2]

**Proof sketch.** Assemble the two tables by inspecting the choice bit and the
two work reads. Every work-read function is recovered from its two coordinates.
The shared table reader's inverse, soundness and erasure laws compose twice;
adding its two 351-bit lower bounds gives the 702-bit guard. -/
private def ndFormat : CodeFormat where
  Code := CodeNDTM
  Table := fun n => CodeTable2 n × CodeTable2 n
  numStates := CodeNDTM.numStates
  assemble := fun n q t => ⟨n, ⟨q, fun b s inp w =>
    (if b then t.2 else t.1) s inp (w 0) (w 1)⟩⟩
  serialize := CodeNDTM.serialize
  tableBits := fun t => codeTable2Bits t.1 ++ codeTable2Bits t.2
  readTable := fun n xs => do
    let (t₀, xs) ← codeReadTable2 n xs
    let (t₁, xs) ← codeReadTable2 n xs
    pure ((t₀, t₁), xs)
  skipTable := fun n => codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipTable2 n) 2
  guard := 702
  fallback := ⟨0, ⟨0, fun _ _ _ _ =>
    ⟨.zero, fun _ => (none, .zero), none, none⟩⟩⟩
  numStates_assemble := fun _ _ _ => rfl
  serialize_assemble := fun _ _ _ => by
    simp [CodeNDTM.serialize, codeTable2Bits, actionBits₂_eq_actionBitsK, workPair]
  assemble_surj := by
    rintro ⟨n, q, tr⟩
    refine ⟨n, q, (fun s inp w₀ w₁ => tr false s inp (workPair w₀ w₁),
      fun s inp w₀ w₁ => tr true s inp (workPair w₀ w₁)), ?_⟩
    congr 1
    congr 1
    funext b s inp w
    have hw : workPair (w 0) (w 1) = w := by
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = 0
      · simp [workPair, hj]
      · have hj' : j = 1 := Fin.ext (by omega)
        simp [workPair, hj']
    cases b <;> simp [hw]
  readTable_append := by
    intro n t xs
    simp only [List.append_assoc, codeReadTable2_append, bind, Option.bind_some, pure]
  readTable_sound := by
    intro n xs t rest h
    simp only [bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
    obtain ⟨⟨t₀, r₀⟩, h₀, ⟨⟨t₁, r₁⟩, h₁, h⟩⟩ := h
    simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rw [codeReadTable2_sound xs t₀ r₀ h₀, codeReadTable2_sound r₀ t₁ r₁ h₁,
      List.append_assoc]
  readTable_erase := by
    intro n xs
    simp only [bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def, pure, Option.map_some,
      codeSkipRepeat, Option.bind_fun_some]
    rw [← codeEraseTable2 n xs, ← codeErase_bind]
    congr 1
    funext p
    simpa only [Option.map_eq_bind, Function.comp_def] using codeEraseTable2 n p.2
  tableBits_length := by
    intro n t
    have h₀ := codeTable2Bits_length t.1
    have h₁ := codeTable2Bits_length t.2
    simp only [List.length_append]
    omega

/-- **An effective nondeterministic code scheme exists** (proved —
phase P3.3): the mirror of `Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode`.

**Proof sketch.** Mirror the deterministic construction
(`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.MathlibBridge`) over the extended record
format: `encode := CodeNDTM.serialize` itself; `decode` parses the
`Turing.pairEncode`d state count, the initial state, and the two transition
tables by the received parser architecture
(`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeParser`, retargeted to the
`Turing.actionBits₂` record — the table is `2 · 27 = 54` records per state
in the fixed enumeration order, two choices by three reads on each of the
input and both work tapes; round-1 finding 3 corrected the earlier `2 · 9`
miscount, and the parser's minimum-length guard scales accordingly), with
the single-state do-nothing machine as the fallback on parse failure and
trailing `true`-padding tolerated by the end-marker discipline
(property 2); the canonizer re-serializes the parsed record by the
**arbitrary-time computability route of the received construction** — the
deterministic `MathlibBridge` explicitly supersedes its polynomial variant,
and `canonizerTime` is an arbitrary bound, so no polynomial ND canonizer is
claimed or needed by this phase's consumers (round-1 finding 4). Fill obligations, named: the record parser and its fallback
totalization; the pad-tolerance lemma (`decode_encode_pad`); the canonizer
assembly and its time bound.

**Fill appendix.** The retargeted parser in the sketch is the shared
`CodeFormat` decoder instantiated by `ndFormat`; no separate parser is needed.
Its table skipper repeats `codeSkipTable2` twice, so `codePrimRepeat` and
`codePrimSkipTable2` establish primitive recursiveness. Apply
`CodeFormat.decode_serialize_pad` for recovery and
`CodeFormat.exists_canonizer` for the deterministic canonizer and its
arbitrary time bound. -/
theorem exists_effectiveNDMachineCode : Nonempty EffectiveNDMachineCode := by
  have hskip : Primrec₂ ndFormat.skipTable :=
    codePrimRepeat codeSkipTable2 codePrimSkipTable2 (fun _ => 2) (Primrec.const 2)
  obtain ⟨canonizer, time, hcanonizer⟩ := ndFormat.exists_canonizer hskip
  exact ⟨{
    encode := CodeNDTM.serialize
    decode := ndFormat.decode
    decode_encode_pad := ndFormat.decode_serialize_pad
    canonizer := canonizer
    canonizerTime := time
    canonizer_computes := hcanonizer }⟩

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/CodeSimulator.lean =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeFormat
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CounterLoop
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Seam
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.VirtualInput
-- B5a continuation: sanctioned imports for the physical binary-header loader.
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputCall

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The uniform code simulator

One format-parameterized simulator for deterministic machine codes: on
`⟨⟨bits t, α⟩, x⟩` it decides whether the machine that `α` denotes halts on `x`
with output exactly `[true]` within `t` steps, in time **one polynomial in
`|α| + |x| + t + 1` jointly**. The parameter is a `Turing.MachineFormat`: a
`Turing.CodeFormat` (12.2c item 8's parse layer) whose codes denote `k`-work-tape
binary machines in the fixed `k`-record serialization. The one-work-tape codes
(`Turing.oneTapeMachineFormat`) and the two-work-tape codes of `Codes2Tape` are
instances; they supply `Turing.exists_uniformMachineCode` (`Diagonalization/EXPCOM`)
and `Turing.exists_uniformMachineCode2` (`Codes2Tape`). [AB09, §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9;
the uniform form required by Example 3.6(3), audited at phase P3.2 round 2]

## Design

* **One interpreter, parameterized by the record grammar.** The table of a
  `k`-tape code is `3^(k+1)` `Turing.actionBitsK` records per state
  (`Turing.tableBitsK`); a single finite machine per format interprets it.
* **Canonize first, then interpret.** The decoded machine's serialization is
  computed in polynomial time (`Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer`):
  the binary state count and the minimum-length guard are checked before any
  state-indexed work, so a huge declared count is never expanded in unary.
* **The clock is §12.7's counter loop** (`Turing.counterLoopTM`) over the
  deadline's binary word; a simulated halt is a live body exit.
* **Status update (fills-8, 2026-10-13): partial.** The two headline contracts
  retain their original admissions. Proved so far:
  - for the canonizer: the native-input binary-header loader and the physical
    fail-fast binary length guard; the canonical-header check, the
    nonoverflowing successor counter and its specialized guard; the guard
    front end, which prepares the header, the successor count and the native
    remainder address from blank tapes, seeks there, runs the guard and seeks
    back on success; and the total two-port parse front end
    (`exists_canonParseFront`), which joins header validity to the guard with
    a fallback rejection port and a ready-for-grammar port, in linear time;
  - for the simulator: the complete generic step block `h1RoundTM`, one finite
    machine per work-tape count `k` whose control is independent of the coded
    state count (record lookup, the selected record's payload, successor
    installation and the round seam), with its exact time bound and head
    envelope (`h1Round_effect`); and the binary deadline clock around it,
    hosted on the virtual input, with its one-bit verdict
    (`h1HostedVerdict_accepts`).

  Still open: the canonizer's restored binary bound, the action-record
  validator, the grammar loop and the emission; the simulator's nested-input
  startup, canonizer installation and joint ledger.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.workReadsK`, `Turing.tableBitsK`, `Turing.serializeK`,
  `Turing.codeSkipTableK` — the fixed `k`-record layout and grammar.
* `Turing.MachineFormat`, `Turing.MachineFormat.toFinTM` — the format parameter.
* `Turing.oneTapeMachineFormat` — the one-work-tape instance.

## Main results

* `Turing.tableBitsK_two`, `Turing.codeSkipTable2_eq_codeSkipTableK` — the
  two-work-tape bridges to `CodeFormat`'s frozen table writer and skipper.
* `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer` — a polynomial-time canonizer.
* `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_uniformSimulator` — the uniform simulator.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9; Example 3.6(3).)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ## The `k`-record layout -/

/-- The fixed enumeration of the work reads of `k` work tapes: tape `0`
outermost, each read over `none`, `some false`, `some true`. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def workReadsK : (k : ℕ) → List (Fin k → Option Bool)
  | 0 => [Fin.elim0]
  | k + 1 => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
      (workReadsK k).map fun r => (Fin.cons w r : Fin (k + 1) → Option Bool)

/-- The fixed serialization of a `k`-work-tape transition table: states in `Fin`
order, then the input read, then the work reads in `Turing.workReadsK` order,
one `Turing.actionBitsK` record each. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def tableBitsK {k n : ℕ}
    (tr : Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → (Fin k → Option Bool) → Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    List Bool :=
  (List.finRange (n + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      (workReadsK k).flatMap fun w => actionBitsK (tr q inp w)

/-- The canonical serialization of a `k`-work-tape binary machine with `n + 1`
states: the binary state count, the unary initial state, the table. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def serializeK {k n : ℕ} (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode n.bits (unaryFin M.q₀ ++ tableBitsK M.tr)

/-- The table skipper of the `k`-record grammar: `n + 1` states of `3^(k+1)`
records each. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipTableK (k n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (List Bool) :=
  codeSkipRepeat ((fun r => codeSkipRepeat r 3)^[k + 1] (codeSkipActionK k n)) (n + 1)

/-- A one-tape read vector built by `Fin.cons` is the constant function. -/
private lemma fin_cons_one (w : Option Bool) :
    (Fin.cons w Fin.elim0 : Fin 1 → Option Bool) = fun _ => w := by
  funext i; fin_cases i; rfl

/-- A two-tape read vector built by `Fin.cons` is the `Turing.workPair` of its entries. -/
private lemma fin_cons_two (w₀ w₁ : Option Bool) :
    (Fin.cons w₀ (fun _ : Fin 1 => w₁) : Fin 2 → Option Bool) = workPair w₀ w₁ := by
  funext i; fin_cases i <;> rfl

/-- The one-work-tape reads are the constant functions, in table order. -/
lemma workReadsK_one : workReadsK 1 =
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).map fun w => fun _ => w := by
  simp [workReadsK, fin_cons_one]

/-- The two-work-tape reads are the `Turing.workPair`s, in table order. -/
lemma workReadsK_two : workReadsK 2 =
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).map fun w₁ => workPair w₀ w₁ := by
  simp [workReadsK, fin_cons_one, fin_cons_two]

/-- At two work tapes the generic table writer is `Turing.codeTable2Bits`. -/
lemma tableBitsK_two {n : ℕ}
    (tr : Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → (Fin 2 → Option Bool) → Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    tableBitsK tr = codeTable2Bits (fun q inp w₀ w₁ => tr q inp (workPair w₀ w₁)) := by
  unfold tableBitsK codeTable2Bits
  rw [workReadsK_two]
  simp only [List.flatMap_assoc, List.flatMap_map]

/-- At two work tapes the generic table skipper is `Turing.codeSkipTable2`. -/
lemma codeSkipTable2_eq_codeSkipTableK (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeSkipTable2 n xs = codeSkipTableK 2 n xs := rfl

/-! ## Machine formats -/

/-- A **deterministic machine format**: a `Turing.CodeFormat` whose codes denote
`k`-work-tape binary machines, serialized in the fixed `k`-record layout and
parsed by the fixed `k`-record grammar. [AB09, §1.4] -/
structure MachineFormat extends CodeFormat where
  /-- the work-tape count of the coded machines -/
  k : ℕ
  /-- the machine a code denotes -/
  machine : (M : Code) → MultiTapeTM k Bool (Fin (numStates M + 1))
  /-- the format's serialization is the fixed `k`-record serialization -/
  serialize_eq : ∀ M, serialize M = serializeK (machine M)
  /-- the format's table skipper is the fixed `k`-record skipper -/
  skipTable_eq : ∀ n xs, skipTable n xs = codeSkipTableK k n xs

/-- The bundled machine a code of a machine format denotes. -/
def MachineFormat.toFinTM (F : MachineFormat) (M : F.Code) : FinTM Bool where
  k := F.k
  State := Fin (F.numStates M + 1)
  tm := F.machine M

/-- The one-tape format's table skipper is the generic skipper at one work tape: the
framed one-tape action skipper is `Turing.codeSkipActionK 1`. -/
private lemma oneTape_skipTable_eq (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    oneTapeFormat.skipTable n xs = codeSkipTableK 1 n xs := by
  have h : codeSkipAction n = codeSkipActionK 1 n :=
    funext (codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK n)
  show codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipAction n) 3) 3) (n + 1) xs = _
  rw [h]; rfl

/-- The frozen one-tape serialization is the generic one at one work tape, record for
record (`Turing.workReadsK_one`, `Turing.actionBits_eq_actionBitsK`). -/
private lemma oneTape_serialize_eq (M : CodeTM) : M.serialize = serializeK M.tm := by
  unfold CodeTM.serialize serializeK tableBitsK
  rw [workReadsK_one]
  simp only [List.flatMap_map, actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]

/-- The one-work-tape code format `Turing.oneTapeFormat` as a machine format.
Its decoder is `Turing.codeDecode` and its bundled machines are
`Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM`, both definitionally. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def oneTapeMachineFormat : MachineFormat :=
  { oneTapeFormat with
    k := 1
    machine := fun M => M.tm
    serialize_eq := oneTape_serialize_eq
    skipTable_eq := oneTape_skipTable_eq }

namespace MachineFormat

variable (F : MachineFormat)

/-! ### Positive grammar bound (B5a fill preparation)

These lemmas justify the extra fail-fast guard even when `F.guard = 0`.
They concern the specified parser; the finite binary implementation and its
polynomial time ledger remain the canonizer's continuation obligation.
-/

/-- Iterated skipping consumes the sum of the per-record lower bounds.

**Proof sketch.** Split off the first successful skip, apply the induction
hypothesis to its suffix, and add the two length inequalities. -/
private lemma skipRepeat_consumes (r : List Bool → Option (List Bool)) (b : ℕ)
    (hr : ∀ xs ys, r xs = some ys → b + ys.length ≤ xs.length)
    (m : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool) (h : codeSkipRepeat r m xs = some ys) :
    b * m + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  induction m generalizing xs with
  | zero =>
    have heq : xs = ys := Option.some.inj h
    simp [heq]
  | succ m ih =>
    obtain ⟨zs, hz, hy⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
    have hfirst := hr xs zs hz
    have hrest := ih zs hy
    rw [Nat.mul_succ]
    omega

/-- Nesting a three-symbol reader multiplies its consumption bound by three. -/
private lemma skipSymbols_consumes (r : List Bool → Option (List Bool)) (b : ℕ)
    (hr : ∀ xs ys, r xs = some ys → b + ys.length ≤ xs.length)
    (j : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool)
    (h : ((fun f => codeSkipRepeat f 3)^[j] r) xs = some ys) :
    b * 3 ^ j + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  induction j generalizing xs ys with
  | zero => simpa using hr xs ys h
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply'] at h
    have hb := skipRepeat_consumes _ (b * 3 ^ j) (fun u v huv => ih u v huv)
      3 xs ys h
    simpa only [Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_assoc] using hb

/-- A successful table skip consumes a positive number of bits per state,
independently of the format's optional guard. -/
private lemma skipTable_consumes (k n : ℕ) (xs ys : List Bool)
    (h : codeSkipTableK k n xs = some ys) :
    (4 * k + 5) * 3 ^ (k + 1) * (n + 1) + ys.length ≤ xs.length := by
  have ha (u v : List Bool) (hu : codeSkipActionK k n u = some v) :
      4 * k + 5 + v.length ≤ u.length := by
    rw [← codeEraseActionK] at hu
    obtain ⟨⟨a, rest⟩, hread, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hu
    rw [codeReadActionK_sound u a rest hread, List.length_append]
    exact Nat.add_le_add_right (codeActionK_length a) _
  exact skipRepeat_consumes _ _ (fun u v huv =>
    skipSymbols_consumes _ _ ha (k + 1) u v huv) (n + 1) xs ys h

/-- A successful scanner satisfies the positive grammar guard already on the
suffix following the binary header. This holds also for a zero format guard.

**Proof sketch.** Decompose the successful scanner into its header, initial-state
and table checks. Erasure and initial-state reader soundness show that the table
input is a suffix of the header remainder. Apply the generic table-skip bound
and discard the nonnegative final-suffix length. -/
private lemma scan_grammar_guard (α bits rest tail : List Bool)
    (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest)) (hs : F.scan α = some tail) :
    (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1) ≤ rest.length := by
  unfold CodeFormat.scan at hs
  rw [hp] at hs
  dsimp only [bind, Option.bind] at hs
  split at hs
  · contradiction
  split at hs
  · contradiction
  obtain ⟨table, hq, ht⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp hs
  obtain ⟨suffix, htable, _⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp ht
  rw [F.skipTable_eq] at htable
  have hlen := skipTable_consumes F.k (codeBitsNat bits) table suffix htable
  rw [← codeEraseFin] at hq
  obtain ⟨⟨q, r⟩, hread, rfl⟩ := Option.map_eq_some_iff.mp hq
  have hword := codeReadFin_sound rest q r hread
  have hrest : r.length ≤ rest.length := by
    rw [hword, List.length_append]
    omega
  dsimp only at hlen
  omega

/-- Reject a binary header whose declared table cannot fit in the remaining
input, before evaluating the format scanner. This is a specification function,
not yet a certified finite-machine implementation. -/
private def guardedScan (α : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode α
  if rest.length < (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)
    then none else F.scan α

/-- The additional positive guard preserves the scanner exactly.

**Proof sketch.** Header failure already fails the scanner. If the new guard
fails, any hypothetical successful scan contradicts `scan_grammar_guard`;
otherwise the guarded scanner calls the original scanner. -/
private lemma guardedScan_eq (α : List Bool) : guardedScan F α = F.scan α := by
  unfold guardedScan
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [CodeFormat.scan, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    dsimp only [bind, Option.bind]
    split
    next hg =>
      cases hs : F.scan α with
      | none => rfl
      | some tail =>
        have := scan_grammar_guard F α bits rest tail hp hs
        omega
    · rfl

/-- Early failure of the positive grammar guard selects exactly the prescribed
fallback, including for a zero guard and a potentially accepting fallback. -/
private lemma decode_of_grammar_guard (α bits rest : List Bool)
    (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest))
    (hg : rest.length < (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)) :
    F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  have hs : F.scan α = none := by
    rw [← guardedScan_eq]
    simp [guardedScan, hp, hg]
  have hparse : F.parseFull α = none := by
    rw [F.scan_full] at hs
    exact Option.map_eq_none_iff.mp hs
  exact F.decode_of_parseFull_none α hparse

/-- Passing the positive guard bounds state-count work by the available input. -/
private lemma grammar_guard_states (n s : ℕ)
    (h : (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (n + 1) ≤ s) : n + 1 ≤ s := by
  have hc : 1 ≤ (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) :=
    Nat.mul_pos (by omega) (Nat.pow_pos (by omega))
  have hs : n + 1 ≤ (4 * F.k + 5) * 3 ^ (F.k + 1) * (n + 1) := by
    simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul_right (n + 1) hc
  exact hs.trans h

/-! ### Physical binary-header loading (B5a continuation) -/

/-- The undoubled header, or the empty word when the pair grammar fails.
The later validation phase must distinguish failure from a valid zero header. -/
private def canonHeader (α : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  ((pairDecode α).map Prod.fst).getD []

/-- Loading a doubled header never produces more bits than the source input. -/
private lemma canonHeader_length (α : List Bool) : (canonHeader α).length ≤ α.length := by
  cases hp : pairDecode α with
  | none => simp [canonHeader, hp]
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨bits, rest⟩
    have he := congrArg List.length (eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode α bits rest hp)
    rw [length_pairEncode] at he
    simp only [canonHeader, hp, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]
    omega

/-- A physical linear-time header loader installs the binary header on tape
zero and restores a clean seam with the original native input available.

**Proof sketch.** Install the public pair-first extractor through the public
native-input call row. The header length is at most the original input length,
so the call row's ledger is linear as well. No parsing or host trace is copied. -/
private lemma exists_canonHeaderCall :
    ∃ (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) (a : ℕ), 0 < C.k ∧
      ∀ α : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ a * (α.length + 1), 0 < t ∧
        (∀ u, 0 < u → u < t →
          (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) u).state ≠
            some exit) ∧
        C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) entry (fun _ => [])) t =
          Cfg.ofWords exit (stateWord C.k (canonHeader α)) := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst
  obtain ⟨C, entry, exit, c, hk, hC⟩ :=
    FinTM.exists_inputCallTM M canonHeader (fun n => a * (n + 1)) hM
  refine ⟨C, entry, exit, c * (a + 2), hk, ?_⟩
  intro α
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩ := hC α
  refine ⟨t, ht.trans ?_, hpos, hcut, hrun⟩
  have hlen := canonHeader_length α
  calc
    c * (a * (α.length + 1) + α.length + (canonHeader α).length + 1) ≤
        c * (a * (α.length + 1) + 2 * (α.length + 1)) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (by omega)
    _ = _ := by ring

/-! ### Physical fail-fast length guard (B5a continuation)

The catalog has whole-input scans but no fixed-block input scan with a short-input
exit. The following body supplies that missing finite controller; the binary
countdown itself is the public `counterLoopTM`, not a new loop implementation.
The body has no work tapes and never emits. Its block length is `b + 1`, so
even the zero-format-guard case can use the positive grammar minimum.
-/

/-- Progress through a fixed positive block; `none` is the short-input exit. -/
private def guardPhase (b u : ℕ) : Option (Fin (b + 1)) :=
  some ⟨u % (b + 1), Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.succ_pos _)⟩

/-- Read at most `b + 1` actual input symbols, returning to the anchor after
one whole block and taking a distinct live exit on a boundary blank. -/
private def guardBlockTM (b : ℕ) : MultiTapeTM 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) where
  q₀ := guardPhase b 0
  tr := fun q inp _ => match q with
    | none => inputMoveAction 0 none
    | some i => if inp.isSome then
        inputMoveAction 1 (guardPhase b (i.val + 1))
      else inputMoveAction 0 none

/-- A block-scan configuration after `j` input cells have been consumed. -/
private def guardCfg (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (q : Option (Fin (b + 1)))
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    Cfg 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) x :=
  ⟨some q, ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩, Fin.elim0, Fin.elim0, out⟩

/-- The finite block controller advances one cell without writing or emitting.
The input-only action law supplies all unchanged configuration fields. -/
private lemma guardBlock_step (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (u j : ℕ)
    (hu : u < b + 1) (hj : j < x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).step (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out) =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b (u + 1)) (j + 1) (by omega) out := by
  have hr := inputSymbolInner
    (cfg := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out) j (by dsimp [guardCfg]; omega) hj
  rw [step_of_inputMoveAction (guardBlockTM b) _ (q' := guardPhase b (u + 1)) 1 rfl (by
    change (if (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out).inputSymbol.isSome then
      inputMoveAction 1 (guardPhase b (u % (b + 1) + 1)) else inputMoveAction 0 none) = _
    rw [hr]
    simp only [Option.isSome_some, if_true, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hu])]
  apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
  · rfl
  · apply Fin.ext
    change (moveInputPos (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) j (by omega) out).inputPos
      SignType.pos).val = j + 1 + 1
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by dsimp [guardCfg]; omega)]
    rfl
  · rfl

/-- Every available prefix of one block is traversed in exactly its length.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the traversed prefix and apply the input-only
one-step contract. The upper bound prevents an intermediate anchor return. -/
private lemma guardBlock_run (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (u : ℕ)
    (hu : u ≤ b + 1) (hlen : j + u ≤ x.length) :
    (guardBlockTM b).runFrom (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) u =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) (j + u) hlen out := by
  induction u with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ u ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega) (by omega)]
    simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using
      guardBlock_step b x u (j + u) (by omega) (by omega) out

/-- At the right input blank, the next transition takes the short-input exit. -/
private lemma guardBlock_blank (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (u : ℕ) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).step
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b u) x.length le_rfl out) =
      guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
  rw [step_of_inputMoveAction (guardBlockTM b) _ (q' := none) 0 rfl (by
    simp [guardBlockTM, guardPhase, Cfg.inputSymbol, guardCfg])]
  simp only [moveInputPos_zero]
  rfl

/-- A short block exits immediately after reading its remaining symbols.
In particular the running time does not depend on the declared state count. -/
private lemma guardBlock_short (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (hshort : x.length - j < b + 1) (out : List Bool) :
    (guardBlockTM b).runFrom (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out)
        (x.length - j + 1) = guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
    guardBlock_run b x j hj out (x.length - j) (by omega) (by omega)]
  have hpos : j + (x.length - j) = x.length := by omega
  simpa only [hpos] using guardBlock_blank b x (x.length - j) out

/-- Exact duration of a block: its fixed size, or the available suffix plus
one transition detecting the blank, whichever is smaller. -/
private def guardTime (b : ℕ) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg 0 Bool (Option (Fin (b + 1))) x) : ℕ :=
  min (b + 1) (x.length + 2 - c.inputPos.val)

/-- Before the end of a block, neither live exit has been reached.

**Proof sketch.** Every strict-interior time is smaller than the block size
and traverses only existing input cells. Its progress index is strictly
positive and below the modulus, so it is neither the anchor nor the failure. -/
private lemma guardBlock_interior (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (u : ℕ) (hu : 0 < u)
    (ht : u < guardTime b (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out)) :
    ∃ s, ((guardBlockTM b).runFrom
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) u).state = some s ∧
      s ≠ guardPhase b 0 ∧ s ≠ none := by
  have hb : u < b + 1 := lt_of_lt_of_le ht (Nat.min_le_left _ _)
  have hl : j + u ≤ x.length := by
    have := lt_of_lt_of_le ht (Nat.min_le_right _ _)
    dsimp [guardCfg] at this
    omega
  rw [guardBlock_run b x j hj out u (by omega) hl]
  refine ⟨guardPhase b u, rfl, ?_, Option.some_ne_none _⟩
  intro he
  have hv := congrArg (fun q => q.map Fin.val) he
  simp [guardPhase, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hb] at hv
  omega

/-- The physical binary guard is the shared counter loop with the block
controller as body. It has exactly one work tape, holding the binary count. -/
private def binaryGuardTM (b : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM 1 Bool (CounterLoopState (Option (Fin (b + 1)))) :=
  counterLoopTM (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) (some none)

/-- Guard entry with the binary counter delimited at the origin. The original
input remains native, so the caller can rewind and parse it after the guard. -/
private def binaryGuardStart (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool) :
    Cfg 1 Bool (CounterLoopState (Option (Fin (b + 1)))) x :=
  counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run))
    (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0

/-- While whole blocks fit, the body orbit advances by their combined length.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the number of blocks. The next full block takes
`b + 1` transitions by `guardBlock_run`, returns its finite progress index to
zero, and preserves the output. This is a body-orbit calculation; the physical
counter is handled solely by the public counter-loop contracts. -/
private lemma guardBlock_orbit (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length) :
    counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r =
      guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) hr out := by
  induction r with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ r ih =>
    have hprev : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length := by
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega
    change (fun c => (guardBlockTM b).runFrom c (guardTime b c))^[r + 1] _ = _
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    change (guardBlockTM b).runFrom
      (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r)
      (guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b)
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out) r)) = _
    rw [ih hprev]
    have ht : guardTime b
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) hprev out) = b + 1 := by
      dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
      rw [Nat.min_eq_left]
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega
    rw [ht, guardBlock_run b x _ hprev out (b + 1) le_rfl (by
      rw [Nat.mul_succ] at hr
      omega)]
    simp only [guardPhase, Nat.mod_self, Nat.zero_mod, Nat.mul_succ, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- Each block is a positive first-return-or-exit segment, including an empty
suffix. This is the hypothesis shared by the returning and escaping host rows. -/
private lemma guardBlock_segment (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out : List Bool) :
    let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
    c.state = some (guardPhase b 0) ∧ 0 < guardTime b c ∧
      (∀ u, 0 < u → u < guardTime b c →
        ∃ s, ((guardBlockTM b).runFrom c u).state = some s ∧
          s ≠ guardPhase b 0 ∧ s ≠ none) := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, guardBlock_interior b x j hj out⟩
  dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
  omega

/-- If the requested whole blocks fit, the physical guard reaches `done`,
silently, in linear time in the input length and the binary counter width.

**Proof sketch.** The body orbit supplies the counter host's first-return
hypotheses. Its exact run is the existing `counterLoopTM_run_done`; its
ledger is `counterLoop_time_le`. Both the number of rounds and their total
input consumption are bounded by the actual input length. -/
private lemma binaryGuard_done (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool)
    (hfit : j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) ≤ x.length) :
    ∃ T ≤ 5 * x.length + 2 * w.length + 2,
      let c := (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T
      c.state = some .done ∧ c.output = out ∧
        c.inputPos.val = j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 1 ∧
        (∀ u < T,
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .done ∧
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .escape) := by
  let d := Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)
  let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
  have hpos (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ d) : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length :=
    (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) hr) j).trans hfit
  have horbit (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ d) :
      counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r =
        guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) (hpos r hr) out :=
    guardBlock_orbit b x j hj out r (hpos r hr)
  let T := (∑ r ∈ Finset.range d,
    guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) +
      counterOverhead w (d + 1)
  have hrun := counterLoopTM_run_done (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) (some none)
    (guardTime b) c w (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0 (by intro p _ _; simp) d rfl
    (by
      intro r hr
      rw [horbit r (by omega), horbit (r + 1) (by omega)]
      obtain ⟨hs, ht, hi⟩ := guardBlock_segment b x _ (hpos r (by omega)) out
      refine ⟨hs, ht, ?_, rfl⟩
      intro u hu hut
      obtain ⟨s, hsu, hsa, hse⟩ := hi u hu hut
      exact ⟨s, hsu, hsa, fun he => hse (Option.some.inj he).symm⟩) T rfl
  have ht := counterLoop_time_le (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c w d rfl (b + 1)
    (fun _ _ => Nat.min_le_left _ _)
  have hd : d ≤ (b + 1) * d := by
    simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul_right d (show 1 ≤ b + 1 by omega)
  refine ⟨T, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [T]
    rw [Nat.mul_comm d (b + 1)] at ht
    dsimp [d] at ht hd ⊢
    omega
  · dsimp only
    have he : (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T = _ := hrun.1
    rw [he, horbit d le_rfl]
    exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, hrun.2.1⟩

/-- If the requested blocks do not fit, the physical guard reaches `escape`
in time independent of the value represented by the binary counter.

**Proof sketch.** Divide the available input length by the positive block
size. Exactly that many full body rounds fit, and the next round detects the
right blank. Apply the public escaping counter-host contract and its prefix
amortization bound; there are at most `|x| + 1` attempted rounds. -/
private lemma binaryGuard_escape (b : ℕ) (x : List Bool) (j : ℕ)
    (hj : j ≤ x.length) (out w : List Bool)
    (hshort : x.length < j + (b + 1) * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    ∃ T ≤ (b + 5) * (x.length + 1) + 2 * w.length,
      let c := (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T
      c.state = some .escape ∧ c.output = out ∧ c.inputPos.val = x.length + 1 ∧
        (∀ u < T,
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .done ∧
          ((binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) u).state ≠
            some .escape) := by
  let r₀ := (x.length - j) / (b + 1)
  let c := guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) j hj out
  have hdiv := Nat.mod_add_div (x.length - j) (b + 1)
  have hmod := Nat.mod_lt (x.length - j) (Nat.succ_pos b)
  have hstart : j + (b + 1) * r₀ ≤ x.length := by dsimp [r₀]; omega
  have hlast : x.length - (j + (b + 1) * r₀) < b + 1 := by
    rw [← Nat.sub_sub]
    change (x.length - j) - (b + 1) * ((x.length - j) / (b + 1)) < b + 1
    rw [← Nat.mod_eq_sub_mul_div]
    exact hmod
  have hr₀ : r₀ < Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) := by
    by_contra hn
    have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) (Nat.le_of_not_gt hn)
    omega
  have hpos (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ r₀) : j + (b + 1) * r ≤ x.length :=
    (Nat.add_le_add_left (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 1) hr) j).trans hstart
  have horbit (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ r₀) :
      counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r =
        guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r) (hpos r hr) out :=
    guardBlock_orbit b x j hj out r (hpos r hr)
  have hexit : counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c (r₀ + 1) =
      guardCfg b x none x.length le_rfl out := by
    change (fun z => (guardBlockTM b).runFrom z (guardTime b z))^[r₀ + 1] c = _
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    change (guardBlockTM b).runFrom
      (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r₀)
      (guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r₀)) = _
    rw [horbit r₀ le_rfl]
    have ht : guardTime b
        (guardCfg b x (guardPhase b 0) (j + (b + 1) * r₀) hstart out) =
        x.length - (j + (b + 1) * r₀) + 1 := by
      dsimp [guardTime, guardCfg]
      omega
    rw [ht]
    exact guardBlock_short b x _ hstart hlast out
  let T := (∑ r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1),
    guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) +
      counterOverhead w (r₀ + 1)
  have hrun := counterLoopTM_run_escape (guardBlockTM b) (guardPhase b 0) none
    (by simp [guardPhase]) (guardTime b) c w (FinTM.bufferTape w) 0
    (by intro p _ _; simp) r₀ hr₀ (by
      intro r hr
      rw [horbit r hr]
      exact guardBlock_segment b x _ (hpos r hr) out)
    (by rw [hexit]; rfl) T rfl
  have hs : (∑ r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1),
      guardTime b (counterLoopOrbit (guardBlockTM b) (guardTime b) c r)) ≤
        (r₀ + 1) * (b + 1) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _r ∈ Finset.range (r₀ + 1), (b + 1) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum (fun _ _ => Nat.min_le_left _ _)
      _ = _ := by simp
  have hc := counterOverhead_le_of_le w (r₀ + 1) (by omega)
  have hn : r₀ + 1 ≤ x.length + 1 := by
    have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right r₀ (show 1 ≤ b + 1 by omega)
    simp only [one_mul] at this
    omega
  refine ⟨T, ?_, ?_⟩
  · calc
      T ≤ (r₀ + 1) * (b + 1) + (4 * (r₀ + 1) + 2 * w.length) :=
        Nat.add_le_add hs hc
      _ = (b + 5) * (r₀ + 1) + 2 * w.length := by ring
      _ ≤ _ := Nat.add_le_add_right (Nat.mul_le_mul_left (b + 5) hn) _
  · dsimp only
    have he : (binaryGuardTM b).runFrom (binaryGuardStart b x j hj out w) T = _ := hrun.1
    rw [he, hexit]
    exact ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, hrun.2.1⟩



/-- The last bit, with the empty word accepted as canonical zero. -/
private def canonBitsOK (w : List Bool) : Bool := w.getLast?.getD true

/-- A last-symbol fold has exactly the finite scan's canonicality verdict. -/
private lemma canonBits_fold (w : List Bool) (a : Bool) :
    w.foldl (fun _ b => b) a = w.getLast?.getD a := by
  induction w generalizing a with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
    simp only [List.foldl_cons, ih, List.getLast?_cons, Option.getD_some]

/-- The parser's binary value is the counter host's binary value. -/
private lemma canonBits_value (w : List Bool) :
    w.foldr Nat.bit 0 = Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) := by
  rw [Nat.ofDigits_eq_foldr, List.foldr_map]
  have step : (fun (bit : Bool) (tail : ℕ) => (bit.toNat : ℕ) + 2 * tail) = Nat.bit := by
    funext bit tail
    cases bit <;> simp [Nat.bit, Nat.add_comm]
  simpa only [Nat.cast_id] using
    congrArg (fun f : Bool → ℕ → ℕ => w.foldr f 0) step.symm

/-- A finite last-bit check suffices to recover the canonical binary word.

**Proof sketch.** Remove the low bit. A nonempty canonical tail has positive
value, so adjoining either low bit is exactly the binary constructor law;
the singleton case admits only the bit one. -/
private lemma canonBits_of_last (w : List Bool) :
    canonBitsOK w = true → (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits = w := by
  induction w with
  | nil => intro _; simp
  | cons b w ih =>
    intro h
    cases w with
    | nil => cases b <;> simp_all [canonBitsOK, Nat.bit]
    | cons c w =>
      have htail : canonBitsOK (c :: w) = true := by
        simpa only [canonBitsOK, List.getLast?_cons_cons] using h
      have he := ih htail
      have hne : (c :: w).foldr Nat.bit 0 ≠ 0 := by
        intro hz
        simp only [hz, Nat.zero_bits] at he
        contradiction
      rw [List.foldr_cons, Nat.bits_append_bit _ b (fun hz => (hne hz).elim), he]

/-- Canonical natural-number digits pass the finite last-bit check.

**Proof sketch.** Use the public binary recursion from zero and one, so every
extension has a nonzero tail. The public decoding identity shows that such
a tail has nonempty digits; its last bit is unchanged by the extension. -/
private lemma canonBits_bits (n : ℕ) : canonBitsOK n.bits = true := by
  refine Nat.binaryRecFromOne (motive := fun m => canonBitsOK m.bits = true)
    (by simp [canonBitsOK]) (by simp [canonBitsOK]) ?_ n
  intro low tail nonzero canonical
  have nonempty : tail.bits ≠ [] := by
    intro hempty
    have decoded := codeBitsNat_bits tail
    rw [hempty] at decoded
    exact nonzero decoded.symm
  rw [Nat.bits_append_bit tail low (fun hz => (nonzero hz).elim)]
  cases htail : tail.bits with
  | nil => exact (nonempty htail).elim
  | cons first rest =>
    simpa only [canonBitsOK, htail, List.getLast?_cons_cons] using canonical

/-- The finite check recognizes exactly the canonical little-endian words. -/
private lemma canonBitsOK_iff (w : List Bool) :
    canonBitsOK w = true ↔ w = (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (canonBits_of_last w h).symm
  · intro h
    calc
      canonBitsOK w = canonBitsOK (w.foldr Nat.bit 0).bits := congrArg canonBitsOK h
      _ = true := canonBits_bits _

/-- A spare high zero makes the state-count successor nonoverflowing. -/
private def canonCount (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (incFixed (w ++ [false])).getD []

/-- Incrementing with a spare high zero preserves the enlarged width and
represents one more than the original header, including the empty header.

**Proof sketch.** Follow the carry through the low one bits. At the first
zero the increment stops; the appended zero guarantees that this happens.
Each recursive carry doubles the value equation. -/
private lemma canonCount_spec (w : List Bool) :
    incFixed (w ++ [false]) = some (canonCount w) ∧
      (canonCount w).length = w.length + 1 ∧
      (canonCount w).foldr Nat.bit 0 = w.foldr Nat.bit 0 + 1 := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [canonCount, incFixed, Nat.bit]
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b with
    | false =>
      simp [canonCount, incFixed, List.foldr_append, Nat.bit]
    | true =>
      have he : canonCount (true :: w) = false :: canonCount w := by
        change ((incFixed (w ++ [false])).map (false :: ·)).getD [] = _
        rw [ih.1]
        rfl
      rw [he]
      simp only [List.cons_append, incFixed, ih.1, Option.map_some,
        List.length_cons, ih.2.1, List.foldr_cons, ih.2.2, Nat.bit]
      simp [Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- The canonical-bit checker is the public two-pass scan, with the last
symbol as accumulator and an identity return pass. -/
private def canonBitsTM (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Bool (ScanPhase Bool) :=
  scanTM k i (scanFold (fun _ b => b)) scanKeep true

/-- The canonicality scan preserves every seam word, the native input
position and the empty output, and avoids both verdict anchors until its
exact linear-time return.

**Proof sketch.** Specialize the public scan contract to the last-bit fold.
Its pure result preserves the scanned word, so the interval rewrite is the
original buffer at every cell. The shared contract supplies both exit cuts. -/
private lemma canonBitsTM_run (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (α : List Bool)
    (w : Fin k → List Bool) :
    (canonBitsTM k i).runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w)
        (2 * (w i).length + 2) = Cfg.ofWords (.done (canonBitsOK (w i))) w ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * (w i).length + 2, ∀ b,
        ((canonBitsTM k i).runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (.fwd true) w) t).state ≠
          some (.done b)) := by
  let d := Cfg.ofWords (input := α) (ScanPhase.fwd true) w
  have h := scanTM_run_ofCfg i (scanFold (fun (_ : Bool) b => b)) scanKeep true
    (w i) d rfl (by intro p _ _; simp [d, Cfg.ofWords])
  rw [scanResult_fold, canonBits_fold] at h
  refine ⟨h.1.trans ?_, h.2.1⟩
  apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
  funext j z
